course_name_original: Análisis e Implementación de Sistemas de Automatización
course_name_en: Analysis and Implementation of Automation Systems
prerequisites: Fundamentals of computer science, communications and computer networks
Identify main parts of automated systems, and application technologies: electrical, pneumatic and hydraulic
Basic knowledge of industrial programmable logic controllers and their application environment
Knowledge and handling of process control concepts and their implementation

learning_outcomes.text: Know the main analysis techniques used in the implementation of process automation and supervision systems, their main characteristics and fields of application.
Correctly apply the concepts for specifying the requirements for the operating, startup, and shutdown modes of a machine or production process.
Know different modeling languages frequently used in industrial automation, their basic characteristics, solutions, and application field.
Implement programming modules: programs, functional blocks, and functions through coding according to the IEC 61131-3 standard.
Acquire effective skills for the development and commissioning of real automation systems.

syllabus_topics: Techniques for analysis of automation and supervision systems.
Control system design. Control architectures: centralized, decentralized, and distributed.
Design and implementation of programming modules. IEC 61131-3 coding.
assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum grade of 5 out of 10 is required for each of the evaluation elements (Cuestionario 1, Cuestionario 2, and Trabajo Final). If these minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as (1/10)*C1 + (2/10)*C2 + (7/10)*TF. Grades obtained in each test may be maintained between calls of the same academic year. In case of doubt regarding authorship or unauthorized means, students may be asked for an in-person defense, failure to attend will result in a 0 for the test.
